Sh. Rupender Singh. vs Rahul Communication. & Anr. on 7 July, 2023
H. P. STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL
 COMMISSION SHIMLA.

 First Appeal No.: 39/2021
 Date of Presentation: 01.09.2021
 Order Reserved on : 12.06.2023
 Date of Decision : 07.07.2023
 ___

Rupender Singh, son of Sh. Udham Singh, resident of Village
Daan, P.O. Baggi, Tehsil Balh, District Mandi, H.P.

For the Respondent No.2: Mr. Ashish Souta Advocate vice Mr.
 Dheeraj Kanwar, Advocate.

Justice Inder Singh Mehta, President

ORDER
Instant appeal is arising out of the order dated

19.09.2019 passed by learned District Consumer Commission,

1Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the order?
Rupender Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
(F.A. No.39/2021)

Mandi, in Consumer Complaint No.132/2018, titled Sh. Rupender

Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
Brief facts of Case:
2. Briefly, the case of the complainant is that

complainant purchased a mobile phone (iPhone SS Silver) for his

personal use from the opposite party No.1/retailer for a sum of

Rs.20,500/- vide bill/cash memo dated 21.09.2016. Warranty of

iphone was of two years from the date of purchase. After few

months, black dots appeared on the screen of phone and phone

used to hang frequently. Matter was reported to the opposite

party No.1/retailer, who retained the phone for repair and after

repairing, the phone was returned to complainant. But it again

stopped functioning. E-mail dated 23.08.2017 was sent to the

opposite parties, but of no use. Defective phone having

manufacturing defect was sold by the opposite party No.1/retailer

to the complainant. The opposite parties indulged in unfair trade

practice and there is deficiency in service. Hence, this complaint.
3. The complaint was contested by the opposite parties

by filing separate replies.
4. Opposite party No.1 (retailer) in its reply has not

disputed that a mobile phone was bought by the complainant on

21.09.2016 by expending Rs.20,500/- and warranty of two years

was extended. There was no manufacturing defect in the phone

and same was never retained by opposite party No.1/retailer for
2
Rupender Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
(F.A. No.39/2021)

repair. There was no deficiency in service or unfair trade practice

on the part of the opposite party No.1.
5. Opposite party No.2/manufacturer in its reply has

submitted that phone in question was purchased by the

complainant from the opposite party No.1, who is not an

authorized dealer of the company/opposite party No.2. One year

warranty issued by the company expired on 20.09.2017.

Complainant was bound by the terms and conditions of warranty.

The complainant is not entitled for replacement of phone or

refund of its value as the said phone was out of warranty. Black

dots appeared on screen due to negligent handling of device by

the complainant. As such the complainant is not entitled for any

relief.
6. No rejoinder has been filed.
7. Thereafter, the parties led evidence in support of their

respective pleadings.
8. After hearing the parties, learned District Commission

dismissed the complaint of the complainant.
9. Feeling aggrieved by the findings given by the

learned District Commission, the appellant/complainant has

preferred the instant appeal before this Commission.
10. We have heard the appellant in person and learned

counsel of the respondents and have also gone through the record

carefully.
3
Rupender Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
(F.A. No.39/2021)
11. The appellant/complainant has submitted that he had

purchased a mobile phone from the opposite party No.1/retailer for

a sum of Rs.20,500/-. After few months, the black dots appeared

on the screen of mobile phone. Thereafter, complainant

approached the opposite party No.1 for repair of mobile phone, but

the same could not be repaired. E-mail dated 23.08.2027 was sent

to the opposite parties, but of no use. The mobile in question was

within warranty period. Therefore, the opposite parties are liable to

compensate the appellant/complainant. The appellant prays that

the appeal of the appellant be allowed and impugned order be set

aside.
12. On the other hand learned counsel for the respondent

No.1 (retailer) has submitted that no expert report was filed by the

complainant to prove his case. The mobile phone which was

brought to the respondent No.1 was not repairable and there is no

liability against the respondent No.1 and prays for the dismissal of

appeal.
13. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2

(manufacturer) has submitted that the respondent No.1/Rahul

Communication is not the authorized dealer of the respondent

No.2. He further submitted that impugned order does not require

any interference and prays for dismissal of appeal.
4
Rupender Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
(F.A. No.39/2021)

FINDING
14. The admitted fact emerging on record is that Apple

iPhone was purchased by the complainant from the opposite party

No.1/retailer vide cash memo dated 21.09.2016 (Annexure-C1) on

payment of Rs.20,500/-.
15. In the instant complaint, the complainant has alleged

that after few months of purchase of the mobile phone, black dots

appeared on the screen of phone and while talking to another

person on phone, the voice started spreading and also that phone

used to hang frequently.
16. The complainant has himself placed on record

Annexure C-2, which is copy of e-mail dated 23.08.2017 sent by

the complainant to the opposite party No.2/manufacturer. In the

said e-mail (Annexure C-2), the complainant has specifically stated

that "I suffered huge loss due to sudden switch of my iPhone."
17. Thus, there is a material contradiction in the plea of the

complainant and e-mail sent by the complainant to manufacturer

which ipso facto indicates that plea set up by the complainant in

the complaint is an afterthought version.
18. Moreover, the opposite party No.1/retailer in its reply

has specifically stated that mobile phone in question was never

retained by opposite party No.1 for repair. Relevant portion of para-

6 of the reply is reproduced as under:-
"The replying opposite-party had never detained
 the said phone for repairs."
5
Rupender Singh vs. Rahul Communication & Anr.
(F.A. No.39/2021)
19. The complainant has nowhere alleged in the

complaint and his affidavit that mobile phone is in possession of

the opposite parties for its repair. Therefore, no deficiency in

service or unfair trade practice can be attributed to the opposite

parties. As such, we find no merit in the instant appeal and the

impugned order does not require any interference.
20. Consequently, the appeal of the appellant/complainant

is dismissed and the impugned order remains upheld.
21. No order as to costs.
22. Certified copy of order be sent to the parties and their

counsel(s) strictly as per rules. File of District Commission along

with certified copy of order be sent back and file of State

Commission be consigned to record room after due completion.

Appeal is disposed of. Pending application(s), if any, also disposed

of.
